source_text: ex isto capite quod agitur consideremus, ubi ait: Commendat autem suam caritatem Deus in nobis, quoniam cum adhuc peccatores essemus, Christus pro nobis mortuus est [n24] . Hoc tu dictum exceptis parvulis vis putari. … Tu autem iam in primo tuo librocontra nos clamans, dixisti: "Christum etiam pro parvulis mortuum"
pass_a_gloss: From this chapter let us consider what is at issue, where he says: But God commends his charity in us, since when we were still sinners, Christ died for us. This you wish to be thought said with little ones excepted. But you already in your first book, crying out against us, said: 'Christ died also for the little ones'.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “Let us consider the point at issue in this chapter, where he says: ‘God commends his love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us’ (Romans 5:8). You want this to be thought said with infants excepted.”
“But you, already in your first book, crying out against us, said: ‘Christ died for infants too.’”

choices.why: Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.

choices.choice: The transcription runs 'libro contra' together ('librocontra'); read as two words.

2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Inline in Pass B; verse text checked against the quoted words.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
